subject: Animation
title: Animation Education Goes Global
description: A quick, practical guide to Animation Education Goes Global.

hook.text: Elite animation schools exist on every continent now, from France's Gobelins to Korea's KAIST to CalArts in the U.S.

buildup.text: These schools produce graduates who work for studios worldwide, creating a truly global talent pipeline.

discovery.text: Online courses and free tools like Blender now let anyone learn animation regardless of geography or wealth.

twist.text: The democratization of education means talent can emerge from anywhere — but jobs still cluster in a few cities.

climax.text: Animation education is globalizing faster than animation employment, creating both opportunity and frustration.

punchline.text: Anyone can learn to animate now. Finding a job is another story.

quiz.question: What challenge does global animation education create?
options: There are too few animation schools worldwide
Education has globalized faster than employment, so talent can emerge anywhere but jobs still cluster in few cities
Online courses have replaced all in-person programs
